items.stem: Define differentiation.
items.answer: The process by which cells take up a permanent shape, size and function
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Differentiation – the process by which cells take up a permanent shape, size and function.

items.stem: The correct order of organisation in a multicellular organism is:
items.answer: cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
items.markingKey: (c) cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.
options: cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism

items.stem: Why do multicellular organisms need tissues?
items.answer: Different functions are carried out more efficiently by groups of specialised cells; tissues allow division of labour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: specialisation. 1 mark: efficiency.

items.stem: Arrange in increasing order of organisation and give an example of each from the human body: organ, cell, organ system, tissue.
items.answer: Cell (neuron) → tissue (nervous tissue) → organ (brain) → organ system (nervous system).
items.markingKey: 1 mark order. 1 mark examples.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Unicellular organisms have tissues.
Reason (R): A tissue is a group of similar cells.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In a potted plant, the roots are in water but the leaves are drooping on a hot day. Which plant tissues are involved and what is going wrong?
items.answer: Xylem is carrying water up, but transpiration through stomata in epidermis is faster than supply; leaf parenchyma cells lose turgidity and droop.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: xylem. 1 mark: stomata/transpiration. 1 mark: turgidity.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The process by which cells take up a permanent shape, size and function."
items.answer: differentiation
items.markingKey: (d) Differentiation is the process by which cells take up a permanent shape, size and function.

items.stem: Plants have more dead supportive tissue than animals because:
items.answer: they are stationary and need strength to stay upright
items.markingKey: (c) they are stationary and need strength to stay upright.
options: they are stationary and need strength to stay upright

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A structure made of different tissues working together for a particular function."
items.answer: an organ
items.markingKey: (c) An organ is a structure made of different tissues working together for a particular function.

items.stem: Growth in plants is limited to certain regions because:
items.answer: dividing (meristematic) tissue is present only there
items.markingKey: (d) dividing (meristematic) tissue is present only there.
options: dividing (meristematic) tissue is present only there

items.stem: Define meristematic tissue.
items.answer: Plant tissue made of actively dividing cells, found at growing regions
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Meristematic tissue – plant tissue made of actively dividing cells, found at growing regions.

items.stem: Which of these is the only dead component of phloem?
items.answer: Phloem fibres
items.markingKey: (b) Phloem fibres.

items.stem: How do guard cells open and close stomata?
items.answer: When guard cells take in water they swell and curve, opening the pore; when they lose water they become flaccid and close it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: swelling opens. 1 mark: losing water closes.

items.stem: Classify these plant tissues as a simple permanent tissue or a complex permanent tissue: phloem, sclerenchyma, collenchyma, xylem.
items.answer: A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, sclerenchyma. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, sclerenchyma. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.

items.stem: Classify these into a component of xylem and a component of phloem: xylem fibres, tracheids, phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma, sieve tubes.
items.answer: A component of xylem: tracheids, xylem fibres. A component of phloem: phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma, sieve tubes.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A component of xylem: tracheids, xylem fibres. A component of phloem: phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma, sieve tubes.

items.stem:
Read: A student examined a thin section of a sunflower stem. She saw small, densely packed cells at the tip with large nuclei; in the middle, large thin-walled cells with spaces; near the corners, cells thickened at the corners; and long tubes with thick walls and no cytoplasm in bundles.
(i) Name the tissue at the tip. (ii) Name the thin-walled cells with spaces. (iii) Which tissue provides flexibility? (iv) Which tissue are the long thick-walled tubes, and what do they carry?
items.answer: (i) Apical meristem. (ii) Parenchyma. (iii) Collenchyma. (iv) Xylem (vessels); water and minerals.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Simple permanent tissue of dead cells with walls thickened by lignin that gives strength."
items.answer: sclerenchyma
items.markingKey: (b) Sclerenchyma is simple permanent tissue of dead cells with walls thickened by lignin that gives strength.

items.stem: Classify these plant tissues as a complex permanent tissue or a simple permanent tissue: phloem, collenchyma, parenchyma, xylem.
items.answer: A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem. A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem. A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma.

items.stem: Which of the following is a component of phloem?
items.answer: sieve tubes
items.markingKey: (b) Sieve tubes is a component of phloem. The others: tracheids – a component of xylem; xylem fibres – a component of xylem; vessels – a component of xylem.

items.stem: A farmer notices that the stem of a plant has been chewed in a ring around it, removing the bark and phloem. What will happen to the roots and why?
items.answer: Food from the leaves cannot reach the roots through phloem, so the roots starve and eventually die (girdling).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: phloem cut. 1 mark: roots starve.

items.stem: Classify these plant tissues as a meristematic tissue or a complex permanent tissue: xylem, phloem, intercalary meristem, cambium.
items.answer: A meristematic tissue: cambium, intercalary meristem. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A meristematic tissue: cambium, intercalary meristem. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.

items.stem: Classify these plant tissues as a meristematic tissue or a complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem, apical meristem, intercalary meristem.
items.answer: A meristematic tissue: apical meristem, intercalary meristem. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A meristematic tissue: apical meristem, intercalary meristem. A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem.

items.stem: Classify these plant tissues as a meristematic tissue or a simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma, intercalary meristem, apical meristem, sclerenchyma.
items.answer: A meristematic tissue: apical meristem, intercalary meristem. A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma, sclerenchyma.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A meristematic tissue: apical meristem, intercalary meristem. A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma, sclerenchyma.

items.stem: Which of the following is a component of xylem?
items.answer: tracheids
items.markingKey: (d) Tracheids is a component of xylem. The others: companion cells – a component of phloem; phloem fibres – a component of phloem; phloem parenchyma – a component of phloem.

items.stem: Which type of muscle is found in the walls of the stomach, intestine and blood vessels?
items.answer: smooth (unstriated) muscle
items.markingKey: (c) Smooth (unstriated) muscle: involuntary, spindle-shaped, uninucleate cells without bands.

items.stem: Bone matrix is hard because it contains:
items.answer: calcium and phosphorus compounds
items.markingKey: (d) calcium and phosphorus compounds.

items.stem: How is the structure of a neuron suited to its function?
items.answer: Long axon conducts impulses over long distances; branched dendrites receive signals from many cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: axon. 1 mark: dendrites.

items.stem: Classify these as a muscular tissue or a nervous tissue: (1) muscle of the stomach wall; (2) brain; (3) biceps muscle; (4) nerves; (5) spinal cord.
items.answer: A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the stomach wall. A nervous tissue: brain; nerves; spinal cord.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the stomach wall. A nervous tissue: brain; nerves; spinal cord.

items.stem: Distinguish between cardiac muscle and striated (skeletal) muscle on the basis of structure, control and location.
items.answer: Cardiac muscle: involuntary, cylindrical, branched, uninucleate cells that contract rhythmically throughout life; found in heart. Striated (skeletal) muscle: voluntary, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells with light and dark bands; found in muscles of limbs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: structure, voluntary/involuntary control, location.

items.stem:
Read: A blood report shows: RBC 4.1 million/mm³ (normal 4.5–5.5), WBC 14 000/mm³ (normal 4000–11 000), platelets 2.5 lakh/mm³ (normal 1.5–4.5).
(i) Which values are outside the normal range? (ii) A high WBC count suggests what? (iii) What function of blood could be affected by the low RBC count? (iv) Which connective tissue type does blood belong to?
items.answer: (i) RBC (low) and WBC (high). (ii) The body is fighting an infection. (iii) Transport of oxygen (possible anaemia). (iv) A fluid connective tissue.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Why does a cut on the skin heal and close over, while a damaged nerve in the spinal cord often does not recover?
items.answer: Skin epithelium has cells that can divide and replace lost cells; mature neurons rarely divide, so damaged nerve cells are not easily replaced.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: epithelial cells divide. 1 mark: neurons do not.

items.stem: A cricketer tears a ligament in the knee while another tears a tendon at the ankle. Which injury affects the connection between two bones, and which between muscle and bone? Why do such injuries heal slowly?
items.answer: Ligament: bone to bone; tendon: muscle to bone. Both are fibrous connective tissues with a poor blood supply, so repair is slow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identification. 1 mark: slow healing reason.

items.stem: Classify these as a nervous tissue or an epithelial tissue: (1) nerves; (2) brain; (3) inner lining of the intestine; (4) outer layer of the skin; (5) lining of kidney tubules.
items.answer: A nervous tissue: brain; nerves. An epithelial tissue: inner lining of the intestine; lining of kidney tubules; outer layer of the skin.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A nervous tissue: brain; nerves. An epithelial tissue: inner lining of the intestine; lining of kidney tubules; outer layer of the skin.

items.stem: Which of the following is an epithelial tissue?
items.answer: inner lining of the intestine
items.markingKey: (a) Inner lining of the intestine is an epithelial tissue. The others: cartilage – a connective tissue; nerves – a nervous tissue; adipose tissue – a connective tissue.

items.stem: Classify these as a connective tissue or a muscular tissue: (1) bone; (2) biceps muscle; (3) tendon; (4) muscle of the stomach wall; (5) blood; (6) muscle of the heart wall.
items.answer: A connective tissue: blood; bone; tendon. A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A connective tissue: blood; bone; tendon. A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a muscular tissue?
items.answer: brain
items.markingKey: (a) Brain is a nervous tissue, not a muscular tissue. Each of the others (biceps muscle, muscle of the heart wall, muscle of the stomach wall) is a muscular tissue.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The cell of nervous tissue with a cell body, dendrites and an axon."
items.answer: a neuron
items.markingKey: (a) A neuron is the cell of nervous tissue with a cell body, dendrites and an axon.

items.stem: A plant stem and an animal limb both need support. Compare how plant tissues and animal tissues provide this support.
items.answer: Plants: dead sclerenchyma fibres and lignified xylem give rigidity; collenchyma gives flexible support. Animals: bone (hard connective tissue) forms the skeleton, cartilage gives flexible support, and ligaments and tendons hold bones and muscles together.
items.markingKey: 1 mark plants. 1 mark animals. 1 mark comparison (dead vs living tissue).

items.stem: Classify these as a muscular tissue or a connective tissue: (1) adipose tissue; (2) cartilage; (3) muscle of the heart wall; (4) tendon; (5) biceps muscle; (6) muscle of the stomach wall.
items.answer: A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall. A connective tissue: adipose tissue; cartilage; tendon.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A muscular tissue: biceps muscle; muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall. A connective tissue: adipose tissue; cartilage; tendon.

items.stem: Why does the heart keep beating even when we are asleep, while we cannot move our arm without thinking?
items.answer: Heart is made of involuntary cardiac muscle controlled automatically; arm muscles are voluntary skeletal muscles that act on signals from the brain.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cardiac involuntary. 1 mark: skeletal voluntary.

items.stem: An aquatic plant like Hydrilla floats while a land plant of the same size would sink. Which tissue helps and how?
items.answer: Aerenchyma—parenchyma with large air cavities—makes the plant buoyant.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: aerenchyma. 1 mark: air spaces give buoyancy.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Animal tissue made of elongated cells that contract and relax to cause movement."
items.answer: muscular tissue
items.markingKey: (b) Muscular tissue is animal tissue made of elongated cells that contract and relax to cause movement.

items.stem: Movement of the arm needs the working together of:
items.answer: muscular, skeletal (bone) and nervous tissues
items.markingKey: (b) muscular, skeletal (bone) and nervous tissues.

items.stem: Explain how different tissues work together when you pick up a book.
items.answer: Nervous tissue carries the message from brain to muscles; skeletal muscles contract; tendons pull the bones; ligaments hold the joints; blood supplies oxygen and food for energy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: nervous. 1 mark: muscle/bone/tendon. (blood optional)

items.stem: Why do athletes need a good blood supply to their leg muscles during a race?
items.answer: Blood (connective tissue) brings oxygen and glucose for respiration and removes carbon dioxide and lactic acid, letting muscles keep working.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: supply. 1 mark: removal.

items.stem: When you touch a hot pan you pull your hand away at once. Name the tissues involved, in order.
items.answer: Nervous tissue (sensory nerve, spinal cord, motor nerve) carries the message; skeletal muscle contracts; tendons and bones move the hand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: nervous. 1 mark: muscle and bone.

items.stem: A runner sprints 100 m. List the tissues involved in (i) receiving the start signal, (ii) moving the legs, (iii) supplying oxygen, and explain how they are coordinated.
items.answer: (i) Nervous tissue (ears to brain). (ii) Skeletal muscle with bones, tendons and ligaments. (iii) Blood (RBC with haemoglobin) and cardiac muscle pumping it. The brain coordinates through nerves.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Plants can stand upright without a skeleton.
Reason (R): Sclerenchyma and xylem give mechanical strength to plants.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Bones alone can move the body.
Reason (R): Muscles pull on bones through tendons.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A plant is kept in red ink for a few hours and a thin section of its stem is seen under a microscope. Which tissue appears red and why?
items.answer: Xylem appears red because it carries water (with the dye) from the roots upwards.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: xylem. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem: Ciliated columnar epithelium in the respiratory tract helps to:
items.answer: push mucus forward and clear the passage
items.markingKey: (c) push mucus forward and clear the passage.
options: push mucus forward and clear the passage

items.stem: Classify these into a component of xylem and a component of phloem: phloem parenchyma, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma, companion cells, sieve tubes, tracheids.
items.answer: A component of xylem: tracheids, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma. A component of phloem: companion cells, phloem parenchyma, sieve tubes.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A component of xylem: tracheids, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma. A component of phloem: companion cells, phloem parenchyma, sieve tubes.

items.stem: The husk of a coconut is made of:
items.answer: sclerenchyma
items.markingKey: (c) sclerenchyma.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Complex tissue that carries water and minerals from the roots to other parts."
items.answer: xylem
items.markingKey: (d) Xylem is complex tissue that carries water and minerals from the roots to other parts.

items.stem: Distinguish between smooth (unstriated) muscle and striated (skeletal) muscle on the basis of structure, control and location.
items.answer: Smooth (unstriated) muscle: involuntary, spindle-shaped, uninucleate cells without bands; found in walls of the stomach, intestine and blood vessels. Striated (skeletal) muscle: voluntary, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells with light and dark bands; found in muscles of limbs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: structure, voluntary/involuntary control, location.

items.stem: Which of the following is a muscular tissue?
items.answer: muscle of the stomach wall
items.markingKey: (a) Muscle of the stomach wall is a muscular tissue. The others: blood – a connective tissue; cartilage – a connective tissue; brain – a nervous tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a connective tissue?
items.answer: outer layer of the skin
items.markingKey: (c) Outer layer of the skin is an epithelial tissue, not a connective tissue. Each of the others (tendon, cartilage, bone) is a connective tissue.

items.stem: What is meant by an organ?
items.answer: A structure made of different tissues working together for a particular function
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An organ – a structure made of different tissues working together for a particular function.

items.stem: Classify these as an epithelial tissue or a connective tissue: (1) cartilage; (2) tendon; (3) lining of kidney tubules; (4) blood; (5) outer layer of the skin.

items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): An epithelial tissue: lining of kidney tubules; outer layer of the skin. A connective tissue: blood; cartilage; tendon.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.

items.answer: A complex permanent tissue: phloem, xylem. A simple permanent tissue: collenchyma, parenchyma, sclerenchyma.

items.answer: A muscular tissue: muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall. A nervous tissue: brain; nerves; spinal cord.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A muscular tissue: muscle of the heart wall; muscle of the stomach wall. A nervous tissue: brain; nerves; spinal cord.

items.stem: Why does the grass grow back quickly after being grazed?
items.answer: Grasses have intercalary meristems at the base of leaves and internodes, which keep dividing.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: intercalary meristem. 1 mark: location.

items.stem: Water reaches the top of a tall tree mainly through:
items.answer: xylem vessels and tracheids

items.answer: Striated (skeletal) muscle: voluntary, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells with light and dark bands; found in muscles of limbs. items.stem: The longest cells in the human body are:
items.answer: nerve cells
items.markingKey: (c) nerve cells.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an epithelial tissue?
items.answer: spinal cord
items.markingKey: (c) Spinal cord is a nervous tissue, not an epithelial tissue. Each of the others (inner lining of the intestine, outer layer of the skin, lining of the mouth) is an epithelial tissue.

items.stem: Which of the following is a component of xylem?
items.answer: vessels
items.markingKey: (b) Vessels is a component of xylem. The others: sieve tubes – a component of phloem; phloem parenchyma – a component of phloem; companion cells – a component of phloem.

items.stem: Distinguish between striated (skeletal) muscle and cardiac muscle on the basis of structure, control and location.
items.answer: Striated (skeletal) muscle: voluntary, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells with light and dark bands; found in muscles of limbs. Cardiac muscle: involuntary, cylindrical, branched, uninucleate cells that contract rhythmically throughout life; found in heart.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: structure, voluntary/involuntary control, location.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Animal tissue made of neurons that receive and conduct impulses."
items.answer: nervous tissue
items.markingKey: (b) Nervous tissue is animal tissue made of neurons that receive and conduct impulses.
